It also supports your EC2 instance if the instance isn\u2019t managed by Systems Manager.\\n\\nWhen you can\u2019t connect to your EC2 instance, [run the AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH automation](https://signin.aws.amazon.com/signin?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fconsole.aws.amazon.com%2Fsystems-manager%2Fautomation%2Fexecute%2FAWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH%3FhashArgs%3D%2523%26isauthcode%3Dtrue%26oauthStart%3D1723225572321%26state%3DhashArgsFromTB_us-east-2_87b69ea9730adeee&client_id=arn%3Aaws%3Asignin%3A%3A%3Aconsole%2Fssmautomation&forceMobileApp=0&code_challenge=L4WRcsIrWdy2WbtELmscw7pu4-_epf2FgBBTyIPs3fo&code_challenge_method=SHA-256) to diagnose the issue and fix it, regardless of whether you installed SSM Agent in your EC2 instance. For more information, see [I'm receiving errors when trying to connect to my EC2 instance using SSH. How can I use the AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH automation workflow to troubleshoot SSH connection issues?](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-ssh-errors-automation-workflow)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/articles/ARALtPJTdWSCSK8R_nwno_0Q/using-saw-to-diagnose-common-issues-in-your-aws-environment\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH\",\"context\":\"# `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH`\\n\\n**Description**\\n\\nThe `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH` runbook installs the Amazon EC2Rescue\\ntool for Linux, and then uses the EC2Rescue tool to check or attempt to fix common\\nissues that prevent a remote connection to the Linux machine via SSH. Optionally,\\nchanges can be applied offline by stopping and starting the instance, if the user\\nexplicitly allows for offline remediation. By default, the runbook operates in\\nread-only mode.\\n\\nRun this Automation (console)\\n\\nFor information about working with the `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH`\\nrunbook, see this `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH` troubleshooting topic from\\nAWS Premium Support.\\n\\n**Document type**\\n\\nAutomation\\n\\n**Owner**\\n\\nAmazon\\n\\n**Platforms**\\n\\nLinux\\n\\n**Parameters**\\n\\n* Action\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Valid values: CheckAll | FixAll\\n\\n Default: CheckAll\\n\\n Description: (Required) Specify whether to check for issues without fixing\\n them or to check and automatically fix any discovered issues.\\n* AllowOffline\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Valid values: true | false\\n\\n Default: false\\n\\n Description: (Optional) Fix only - Set it to true if you allow an offline\\n SSH remediation in case the online troubleshooting fails, or the provided\\n instance is not a managed instance. Make sure the bucket\\n policy does not grant unnecessary read/write permissions to parties that do\\n not need access to the collected logs.\\n* SubnetId\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Default: SelectedInstanceSubnet\\n\\n \\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-awssupport-troubleshootssh.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot \\\"Connection refused\\\" or \\\"Connection timed out\\\" errors when I use SSH to connect to my Amazon EC2 instance?\",\"context\":\"### Troubleshoot issues with instances that pass their status checks\\n\\n**Run the AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH runbook to automatically resolve issues**\\n\\nTo automatically identify and resolve SSH issues, [run the AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH runbook](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-ssh-errors-automation-workflow). The runbook installs the EC2Rescue tool on your instance to identify and fix issues that block a remote SSH connection to a Linux host.\\n\\n**Manually troubleshoot OS-level issues**\\n\\nUse the [EC2 Serial Console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-serial-console.html) or Session Manager, a capability of AWS Systems Manager, to connect to your instance. Then, troubleshoot SSH configuration issues.\\n\\nTo use the EC2 Serial Console, you must use a [supported instance type](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-serial-console-prerequisites.html#sc-prereqs-instance-types) and [configure access to the serial console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configure-access-to-serial-console.html). You can also use the EC2 Serial Console to troubleshoot OS-level issues such as boot issues and network configuration issues.\\n\\nTo use Session Manager, your instance must be a [managed node](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/managed_instances.html) and must meet the [Session Manager prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-prerequisites.html). Also, the attached AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role must have [AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.html) permissions.\\n\\nTo update your configuration so that it doesn't block SSH access, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. [Use the EC2 Serial Console to connect to the instance](https\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-linux-resolve-ssh-connection-errors\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"How do I resolve SSH connection issues to my Amazon EC2 Linux instance?\",\"context\":\"### Run the AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH runbook\\n\\n**Prerequisites:**\\n\\n* Copy the **instance ID** of the unreachable instance.\\n* Make sure that you have the required AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions. Or, [use the AWS Systems Manager console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/running-simple-automations.html#simple-console) and configure the following settings:\\n\\n* For **Automation document**, choose **AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH**.\\n* Under **Document details**, choose **Default version at runtime** for **Runbook version**.\\n* Under **Input parameters**, enter the unreachable instance's ID for **InstanceID** and **FixAll** for **Action**.\\n\\nFor more information, see [Smart RDP and SSH remediation with AWS Systems Manager Automation API actions](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/smart-rdp-and-ssh-remediation-with-aws-systems-manager-automation-api-actions/)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-linux-ssh-troubleshooting\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Reset passwords and SSH keys on EC2 instances\",\"context\":\"## How it works\\n\\nTroubleshooting an instance with Automation and the\\n`AWSSupport-ResetAccess` runbook works as follows:\\n\\n* You specify the ID of the instance and run the runbook.\\n* The system creates a temporary VPC by deploying the\\n EC2Rescue CloudFormation stack.\\n* The system identifies a subnet for your temporary VPC in the same\\n Availability Zone as your original instance.\\n* The system launches a temporary, SSM-enabled helper\\n instance.\\n* The system stops your original instance, and creates a backup. It\\n then attaches the original root volume to the helper\\n instance.\\n* The system uses Run Command to run EC2Rescue on the helper instance.\\n On Windows, EC2Rescue enables password generation for the local\\n Administrator by using EC2Config or EC2Launch on the attached,\\n original root volume. On Linux, EC2Rescue generates and injects a\\n new SSH key and saves the private key, encrypted, in Parameter Store. When\\n finished, EC2Rescue reattaches the root volume back to the original\\n instance.\\n* The system creates a new Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of your instance, now\\n that password generation is enabled. You can use this AMI to\\n create a new EC2 instance, and associate a new key pair if\\n needed.\\n* The system restarts your original instance, and terminates the\\n temporary instance. The system also terminates the temporary VPC and\\n deletes the EC2Rescue CloudFormation stack created at the start of the\\n automation.\\n* **Windows**: Your instance generates\\n a new password you can decode from the Amazon EC2 console using the\\n current key pair assigned to the instance.\\n\\n **Linux**: You can SSH to the\\n instance by using the SSH key stored in Systems Manager Parameter Store as\\n **/ec2rl/openssh/`instance\\n ID`/key**\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-ec2reset.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up AWS SSH troubleshooting Automation runbooks"}

**Primary runbook: `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH`**
- It installs EC2Rescue for Linux and checks for, or fixes, common problems that block SSH. It works whether or not SSM Agent is installed on the instance.
- It runs read-only by default.
- Key parameters:
  - `InstanceId` (required).
  - `Action`: `CheckAll` (the default) only diagnoses. `FixAll` diagnoses and applies fixes.
  - `AllowOffline`: defaults to `false`. When `true`, and online troubleshooting fails or the instance isn't SSM-managed, it stops the instance and creates an AMI before changing anything.
  - Optional `S3BucketName` for logs and `AutomationAssumeRole`.
- Run it first with `Action=CheckAll`, review the findings, then decide whether to use `FixAll`.
- `AllowOffline=true` means downtime. Instance-store data is lost on a stop, and a public IP that isn't an Elastic IP will change.

**Network checks: `AWSSupport-ConnectivityTroubleshooter`**
- A connection timeout (rather than "connection refused" or "permission denied") usually means the packets never reach sshd. Common causes are a security group, network ACL, route table or internet gateway problem, or a missing public IP.
- This runbook checks security groups, network ACLs and route tables between two endpoints in a VPC. That includes paths through an internet gateway, a NAT gateway or VPC peering.
- It needs a private `SourceIP` inside your VPC, a `DestinationIP` and a `DestinationPort` of 22. If you're connecting from the internet or on-premises, it's less direct. Checking the instance's security group inbound rule for port 22 from your source IP, plus the subnet's route table and NACL, covers the same ground.

**Other options**
- **`AWSSupport-ResetAccess`** is for lost or incorrect keys. It stops the instance, injects a new SSH key and stores it in Parameter Store. It won't fix a timeout, and it causes downtime.
- **EC2 Serial Console or Session Manager** let you get onto the instance to inspect sshd, firewall rules (iptables/firewalld) and `hosts.allow`/`hosts.deny`. Session Manager needs SSM Agent and the right IAM role. The serial console needs a supported instance type and a password-based sudo user.
